description: The physics behind games and interactive simulations: kinematics and numerical integration, forces and Newton's laws, particles and springs, collision detection and response, rigid body dynamics with constraints, fluids and cloth, and keeping simulations stable and deterministic. Every method is derived, then implemented and visualised in a browser physics sandbox where students compare integrators, break simulations on purpose and tune them to run in real time on a phone.
modelledOn: Bridson, Fluid Simulation for Computer Graphics
outcomes: Model motion with vectors and kinematics and implement explicit, semi-implicit and higher-order numerical integrators.
Apply Newton's laws to compute forces such as gravity, drag, friction and springs and simulate particle systems.
Detect collisions and resolve them with impulses, restitution and friction for particles and rigid bodies.
Simulate rigid body dynamics in 2D and 3D, including rotation, inertia tensors, contacts and joint constraints.
Implement mass-spring cloth and particle-based fluids and explain the trade-offs between accuracy and speed.
Analyse the stability, energy behaviour and determinism of a simulation and design it for networked and replayable games.

units.title: Vectors, kinematics and the simulation loop
topics: Vector algebra for physics: dot and cross products, projections, normalisation and coordinate frames
Kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration; projectile motion and analytic solutions
The physics step inside the game loop: fixed time steps, accumulators and rendering interpolation
Units, scales and choosing world dimensions for a game; floating-point precision

units.title: Numerical integration
topics: Ordinary differential equations as the model of motion; initial value problems
Explicit Euler, semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler and velocity Verlet; local and global error
Runge-Kutta methods (RK2, RK4) and when the extra cost is worth it
Stability: stiff systems, the effect of step size, energy drift and damping
Implicit integration for stiff springs; position-based approaches as an alternative
Comparing integrators on an orbit and a spring and plotting energy over time

units.title: Forces and Newton's laws
topics: Newton's three laws, mass and momentum; force accumulation in an engine
Gravity, drag (linear and quadratic), buoyancy and friction (static and kinetic)
Force generators and registries; game-tuned forces versus physically accurate ones
Projectiles and vehicles: a thrown ball, a bicycle on a laterite road, an okada braking

units.title: Particles and springs
topics: Particle systems: emitters, lifetimes and effects such as smoke, fire, dust and rain
Hooke's law, damped springs and critical damping; bungees and anchored springs
Mass-spring networks: structural, shear and bending springs; soft bodies
Stiff springs and instability; fake springs and position constraints
Rods, cables and simple particle contact constraints
Building a rope bridge or a hanging chain in the sandbox

units.title: Collision detection for physics
topics: Broad phase and narrow phase: bounding volume hierarchies, grids and sweep and prune
Contact generation: sphere, box and plane tests, the separating axis theorem and contact manifolds
GJK and EPA for convex shapes; penetration depth and contact normals
Continuous collision detection and time of impact against tunnelling

units.title: Collision response
topics: Impulse-based response: relative velocity, coefficient of restitution and conservation of momentum
Friction impulses and the Coulomb friction cone
Resolving interpenetration: projection, Baumgarte stabilisation and slop
Resting contact, stacking and sleeping bodies
Simulating a game of marbles or oware seeds bouncing in a board

units.title: Rigid body dynamics
topics: Rotational kinematics: angular velocity, orientation as angles, matrices and quaternions
Torque, angular momentum, moment of inertia and the inertia tensor in world and body space
Integrating rigid bodies in 2D and 3D; normalising quaternions and avoiding drift
Contacts on rigid bodies: impulses at contact points and the effect on spin
Constraints and joints: distance, hinge, ball and socket; sequential impulse solvers and warm starting
Building a 2D rigid body engine with stacking boxes and a ragdoll

units.title: Fluids and cloth
topics: Cloth as a mass-spring system and with position-based dynamics; collisions and self-collision
Fluid models: Eulerian grids versus Lagrangian particles; the Navier-Stokes equations in outline
Smoothed particle hydrodynamics: kernels, density, pressure and viscosity
Grid-based smoke and water: advection, diffusion and pressure projection (stable fluids)
Height-field water and other cheap approximations for phones
Simulating a flag in the wind or kente cloth draped over a figure

units.title: Stability and determinism
topics: Sources of instability: large time steps, stiff constraints, mass ratios and accumulated error
Determinism: floating-point differences across devices, fixed-point arithmetic and fixed update order
Deterministic lockstep and rollback netcode for multiplayer; replays from recorded input
Performance: island partitioning, sleeping, solver iterations and budgets on low-end phones
Capstone: a physics-driven browser game with a documented, stable and deterministic simulation

schedule.title: Vectors, kinematics and the game loop
schedule.exercise: Short problem set: compute a projectile's range with vectors, then explain why a fixed time step with an accumulator is better than a variable one.

tasks.title: Compute dot and cross products of two vectors, project one onto the other and plot the vectors and projection
Simulate a thrown ball with a fixed time step, compare its landing point with the analytic solution and report the error
Implement a fixed-step loop with an accumulator and render interpolation, then show the motion stays smooth when frame rate varies from 20 to 120 fps

schedule.title: Numerical integration
schedule.exercise: Hand-calculate three steps of explicit Euler, semi-implicit Euler and RK4 for a spring and compare with the exact solution.

tasks.title: Write the equation of motion of a mass on a spring as a first-order system and plot its exact solution for given initial conditions
Implement explicit Euler, semi-implicit Euler and velocity Verlet for a spring and plot position error against the exact answer
Implement RK2 and RK4, then find the step size where RK4's extra cost per step is repaid by a larger allowed step

schedule.title: Stability and integrator comparison
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page recommendation on which integrator to use for a game orbit and for a stiff spring, supported by your energy plots.

tasks.title: Increase the step size on a stiff spring until explicit Euler blows up and record the step size at which it first fails
Implement implicit Euler for a stiff spring and compare its stability and energy loss with explicit Euler at a large step
Compare four integrators on a planetary orbit over 100 periods, plot total energy against time and rank the integrators by drift

schedule.title: Forces and Newton's laws
schedule.exercise: Work out terminal velocity for a falling object with linear and quadratic drag, then compare it with a simulation.

tasks.title: Apply Newton's second law to a 5 kg block under three forces, sum the forces and plot its velocity for ten seconds
Add quadratic drag and friction to a sliding crate and verify the terminal velocity and stopping distance against the formulae
Simulate an okada braking on a wet laterite road with tyre friction and compute the stopping distance at 30, 50 and 70 km/h

schedule.title: Particles and springs
schedule.exercise: Tune a damped spring to be critically damped and describe how you would build a fire effect with a particle system.

tasks.title: Build a particle emitter with lifetimes, random velocities and gravity, and render a smoke plume that fades as particles age
Plot the response of a damped spring for under, critical and over damping and find the damping coefficient that is critical
Build a soft-body square from a mass-spring network with structural, shear and bending springs and show it keeps its shape when dropped

schedule.title: Constraints and the rope bridge
schedule.exercise: Short design: explain why a rope bridge made of stiff springs explodes and how position constraints avoid it.

tasks.title: Make a spring chain unstable by raising its stiffness, then stabilise it by reducing the step size and by adding damping
Replace springs with distance constraints in a hanging chain and relax them with a fixed number of iterations per frame
Build a rope bridge with ten planks that holds a rolling ball, stays stable for 60 seconds and breaks when the load exceeds a limit

schedule.title: Collision detection
schedule.exercise: Draw a bounding volume hierarchy for eight objects and write the separating axis test for two boxes in 2D.

tasks.title: Implement a uniform grid broad phase for 500 circles and count how many narrow-phase tests it avoids compared with testing every pair
Implement the separating axis theorem for two rotated boxes in 2D and return the contact normal and penetration depth
Show a fast ball tunnelling through a thin wall with discrete detection, then fix it using swept collision and the time of impact

schedule.title: Collision response and the marbles game
schedule.exercise: Calculate the post-collision velocities of two marbles by hand and then check a simulation of the same case conserves momentum.

tasks.title: Compute the impulse and resulting velocities for a head-on collision between two balls for restitution values 0, 0.5 and 1
Add Coulomb friction impulses to a block sliding on a ramp and verify that it stops when friction exceeds the tangent force
Simulate seeds dropped into an oware board with restitution and friction, count how many settle in each pit and keep a stack stable for 10 seconds

schedule.title: Rigid body rotation
schedule.exercise: Compute the moment of inertia of a plank and a disc, and write a note on why quaternions need normalising.

tasks.title: Compute moment of inertia for a rod, a disc and a box and find the angular acceleration for a given torque
Represent an orientation as a matrix, an angle and a quaternion, rotate a vector with each and confirm the three results agree
Integrate a spinning rigid body in 3D with quaternions for 10,000 steps and show that drift stays small only if you renormalise

schedule.title: Contacts, joints and the ragdoll
schedule.exercise: Design a ragdoll joint layout of eleven bones and list the joint type and angular limits for each joint.

tasks.title: Apply an impulse at an off-centre contact point of a box and check that the resulting spin matches the cross product of the offset and impulse
Build a hinge joint pendulum with a sequential impulse solver and compare the swing period with the analytic value
Build a 2D rigid body engine with stacking boxes and a ragdoll, and make a pyramid of ten boxes sleep without jitter

schedule.title: Cloth and fluids
schedule.exercise: Describe the differences between grid and particle fluids in half a page, and say which suits a phone game.

tasks.title: Create a cloth from a grid of particles pinned at two corners and show it hangs and sways under gravity with structural springs
Write the incompressible Navier-Stokes terms in outline and identify which term each of advection, pressure and viscosity corresponds to
Implement smoothed particle hydrodynamics with density, pressure and viscosity for 500 particles and keep a dam break stable

schedule.title: Flags, smoke and cheap water
schedule.exercise: Choose a fluid or cloth method for three phone game effects and justify each choice with a performance estimate.

tasks.title: Implement stable-fluids advection and diffusion on a 64x64 grid and watch smoke from a source drift in a steady wind
Build a height-field water surface with wave propagation and a boat that floats on it, and keep it running at 60 fps
Simulate a flag in the wind with a position-based cloth, wind force that varies in time and a pole collision, and keep it stable

schedule.title: Stability, determinism and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone deliverable: a design note documenting your game's fixed step, solver iterations, determinism strategy and performance budget.

tasks.title: Find the largest time step and mass ratio at which a stack of five boxes stays stable and record where it first jitters
Run the same simulation in floating point and in fixed point, show where they diverge and make a replay reproduce exactly from recorded input
Build a physics-driven browser game with a fixed step, sleeping bodies and a deterministic replay, and prove two runs match frame by frame
